patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — AWeber and Customer.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

AWeber and Customer.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose AWeber only if your buying job matches “Creator- and SMB-focused email marketing with free forever, Lite/Plus tiers, and landing p” rather than Customer.io's shape. Choose Customer.io only if your buying job matches “Product-led event-driven messaging across email, push, SMS, and in-app — MAP-adjacent to c” rather than AWeber's shape. Workflow advantage: AWeber leans small-business-campaigns; Customer.io leans marketing-automation. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — AWeber and Customer.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: AWeber is Creator- and SMB-focused email marketing with free forever, Lite/Plus tiers, and landing pages.; Customer.io is Product-led event-driven messaging across email, push, SMS, and in-app — MAP-adjacent to classic ESPs..
- Company-size focus: AWeber (micro, small-business) vs Customer.io (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: AWeber-leaning small-business-campaigns vs Customer.io-leaning marketing-automation.
- Researched limits: AWeber — Free: 1 list, limited automations/landing pages, AWeber branding, hard 500-sub / 3k-send caps; Customer.io — Essentials from $100/mo — not an SMB freemium ESP.

Limitations — AWeber: Free: 1 list, limited automations/landing pages, AWeber branding, hard 500-sub / 3k-send caps; Lite caps lists, LPs, automations, users, and segments vs Plus; Customer.io: Essentials from $100/mo — not an SMB freemium ESP; Event/profile model requires product data maturity.

Poor-fit cases: AWeber is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free: 1 list, limited automations/landing pages, AWeber branding, hard 500-sub / 3k-send caps · Customer.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Essentials from $100/mo — not an SMB freemium ESP · Avoid AWeber if you actually need Customer.io's motion (Product-led event-driven messaging across email, push, SMS, and in-app — MAP-adj)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
